<!--
A published article carries a masthead at the head of its first page: the
journal's logo at the left with its name opposite, a rule under both, and the
copyright and the issn at the left beneath it with the issue and the doi at the
right. apaquarto's typst format has set one for a while; the plain LaTeX format
had none.

The band spans the page, which in two columns only the optional argument of
\twocolumn can do, so the masthead is what asks for two columns rather than
\apatwocolumn. A journal document with no journal metadata takes the older
path, which the other two latex-jou fixtures cover.

A successful run produces the masthead above both columns of the first page,
with every field in it, and the article's own text underneath.
-->

# Method

Text of the article, under the masthead.
